newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks find only tiny amount of Jewish funds.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks find only tiny amount of Jewish funds.

text.p: Funds owned by Jewish victims of the Holocaust made up only a tiny part of the unclaimed wealth Swiss banks have found as they pore over claims for dormant accounts on their books, an official said on Tuesday.

"It was around 11,000 Swiss francs ($8,750)," banking ombudsman Hanspeter Haeni told reporters when asked how much Jews had held of the 1.6 million Swiss francs ($1.3 million) in dormant wealth covered by claims submitted recently and judged valid.

Juding from their names, Jews held five of the 11 dormant accounts for which valid claims have been submitted recently, said Haeni, who is coordinating Swiss banks' search for unclaimed assets of people persecuted by Nazi Germany.

Three of them were Jews murdered in Hitler's drive to exterminate European Jewry, he said. Two more were Romanian Jews dispossessed during the war by discriminatory legislation, he said without naming them or the banks involved.

Haeni said in the other six cases, it was either unclear whether the orignial owner was a Jew or else it was obvious from the dates of activity that that account became dormant before or long after the Holocaust.

It was not clear from Haeni's presentation how much of the 1.6 million francs covered by valid claims was already reported by banks. The Swiss Bankers Association has said 38.7 million francs ($30.7 million) in dormant accounts was still lodged in Swiss banks that had lost contact with the original owners.
